title: GFL vs GFM Fault Response
subtitle: Inverter current during a 3-phase fault · 60 Hz · peak per-unit
hook: During a fault, a grid-following inverter needs a voltage to follow. A grid-forming one makes its own. Watch what happens to their current.
outro: Close to the inverter, the PCC voltage collapses: the GFL loses its PLL angle and blocks; the GFM keeps feeding current at its limit.
Without a current limit a GFM would push 3–6 pu: the limiter, not X<sub>v</sub>, sets its contribution to deep faults.
For shallow, remote dips the GFM current is set by its virtual impedance X<sub>v</sub>; the GFL by its K-factor.
interactiveNote: Averaged EMT model · SCR 5 · I<sub>max</sub> 1.2 pu
